subject: Urgent: 5xx/429 spike after model rollout - immediate remediation
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform Reliability Team <platform-reliability@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Marissa,

We started seeing an increase in 5xx and 429 responses for our production inference calls after the 02:00 UTC model rollout this morning. Latency has jumped ~3x on median, and about 12% of requests are now timing out or returning 5xx/429. Our retry logic amplified load and we've seen a retry storm behind the spike. This is impacting our customer-facing search indexer (batch job) and live product traffic.

Attached are a small sample of failed request logs and client-side traces (acme_error_samples_20260620.log). Can you confirm if a new quantization/kernel/serving variant was pushed today? We need an ETA for mitigation or rollback.

—Sara
Sara Klein
Director, Platform Reliability
ACME Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Reliability Team <platform-reliability@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. I’m escalating this to our SRE and inference teams and we’re treating it as P1.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ve looped in Rishi and Dylan to triage now.
- We’ll stand up a short bridge (15m) and propose either a fast rollback to the previous model variant or traffic rerouting to Dedicated capacity if needed.
- I’ll send status updates every 30 minutes until we have a stable mitigation.

Can you share approximate traffic % this customer flow represents for you (p95 qps) and whether you can taper client retries for the next 30 mins? That will help us avoid further amplification.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Fyi — ACME reports elevated 5xx/429 and latency after today’s rollout. They provided client traces. Customer impact: search indexing & live traffic. Suggested immediate actions: investigate serving variant (quantization/profile/kernel), check kernel selection change at 02:00 UTC, consider emergency rollback.

Please coordinate on-call and let me know if we should cut traffic to previous model variant. Evelyn — this is headed for exec attention; we may need a discretionary credit if rollback affects SLA.

--Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Observations from the initial triage (logs + metrics):
- Rollout at 02:00 UTC pushed model v3.1 with a new 4-bit quantization profile and an updated CUDA kernel selector.
- We’re seeing a pattern of KV cache evictions and larger-than-expected memory spikes on infer nodes for this model, leading to slow scheduler responses and transient 5xx.
- 429s correlate with our rate limiter when request bursts hit nodes under GC pressure; client-side retries are causing request pileups (retry storm).

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Emergency rollback to model v3.0 (deployed and validated) — fastest and lowest risk.
2) Traffic split: route ACME traffic to Dedicated pool (if capacity available) while we debug.
3) Increase per-node concurrency throttles and enable an adaptive circuit-breaker for the affected route — buys time but doesn't remove the buggy kernel.

I’m attaching a diagnostic bundle (redwood_diagnostics_20260620.tar.gz) with heap profiles and node logs. I recommend rollback unless Product insists on keeping the variant live.

Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Quick add from runtime: we changed kernel selection heuristics to favour a new fused-attn kernel for seq_len<=256. Load test coverage for the quantized path was limited; looks like the fused kernel interacts badly with 4-bit paths on some GPUs (reported on two instance pools).

Short-term actions I can execute now (ETA ~15-25m):
- Push traffic pin for ACME route to model v3.0 (config-only change, no infra rollout).
- Disable the fused-attn kernel selector for the affected pools (requires config + quick test).
- Patch token bucket retry guidance: set client Retry-After and backoff hints in gateway responses.

I’ll prepare the rollback_plan.md and execute after Marissa confirms ACME is available for a brief failover window.

—Dylan
Inference Engineer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Agree with rollback. We did a gradual rollout but the canary sampling missed this GPU/kernel interaction. Action items:
- Approve immediate rollback to v3.0 for all production traffic for this model family.
- After rollback, schedule post-mortem to update rollout gating (add GPU+quantization integration tests).
- Prepare customer communication and an offer of a one-month credit for impacted SLAs.

Evelyn — can you sign off on credits if ACME escalates to procurement?

Jonas
Senior PM, Serving
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Reliability Team <platform-reliability@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 after latest model rollout - urgent

Sara — update from our side: we have initiated an emergency rollback to model v3.0 for the impacted model family and pinned your route to the previous variant. Early metrics show error rates dropping and median latency returning toward baseline.

What to expect next 60m:
- We will continue to monitor the Datadog dashboard (https://dashboards.datadog.com/board/redwood/acme-5xx-429-spike).
- Rishi and Dylan will follow up with a short post-mortem and a remediation plan that includes stricter rollout gating and a fix for the fused-attn+4-bit path.
- We'll share final diagnostic artifacts and a proposed credit for downtime. Attachments: rollback_plan.md (plan + checklist) and the diagnostics bundle.

Thanks for patience and for slowing client retries — that materially helped reduce the retry storm. I’ll keep you posted when we close the incident.

Best,
Marissa
On Sat, Jun 20, 2026 at 09:15 AM -0700, Sara Klein <sara.klein@acme.com> wrote:
> Marissa,
>
> Quick follow up — current p95 qps for the affected flow is ~210. We have temporarily reduced retries to 1 and put a client-side 10s backoff. Keeping our engineering team on standby for the failover window.
>
> —Sara
